To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the breakthrough curves of VOCs in a fixed bed of zeolite can be simulated with a good accuracy by the LDF model.

we found that mass transfer in VOC adsorbtion on zeolite can be simulated with the Linear Driving Force Model and that we found a relationship between intrapellet mass transfer coefficient, equilibrium constant and average effective diffusivty.

the breakthrough curve of a VOC in a packed column can be predicted using the Linear Driving Force (LDF) model, and that the effective diffusivity of the adsorbed phase can be calculated from the adsorption equilibrium constant and the mass-transfer coefficient.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adsorption of volatile compounds on hydrophobic zeolites and the prediction of breakthrough curves.
the study of the mass transfer of VOCs in adsorption processes.
the adsorption of volatile organics on zeolites and the use of the resulting breakthrough curves for the prediction of adsorption capacities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mass-transfer coefficient is a function of the equilibrium constant, and the effective diffusivity of the adsorbate in the zeolitic matrix, which is independent of the nature of the pollutant.
mass transfer in zeolite adsorption beds is mainly due to intrapellet diffusion and that this process is not affected by the nature and amount of VOCs.
the Linear Driving Force Model is a very good approximation to the mass transfer of VOC in adsorption by zeolite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the adsorption of VOCs on hydrophobic zeolite is a process that can be described by the linear driving force model with an internal mass-transfer coefficient that is a function of the equilibrium constant.
the mass transfer in adsorption of VOCs on zeolites can be modeled with an effective diffusivity independent of the nature of the pollutant.
a simple linear driving force model is adequate to describe the mass-transfer process in the adsorption of VOCs on zeolite.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adsorption of volatile organics is a very fast process.
a constant effective diffusivity can be assumed for the whole range of VOCs adsorption on zeols.
the adsorption of VOCs on zeolites is controlled by intrapellet mass transfer.
